title: Mini HUD: Cost-Latency Correlation & Token Flow for Route+Model
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Design a compact, embeddable HUD (head-up display) component for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-route and per-model correlations between latency, token usage, and cost in a single glance. It should be usable inside route detail pages and as a flyout on aggregated dashboards. Motivation: customers operating at scale want to quickly identify high-cost, high-latency model-route combinations without drilling through full dashboards. The Mini HUD aims to reduce investigative time by surfacing correlated anomalies and providing direct actions (open rollout, pin model variant, open request traces). Scope: - Compact visual summary (single-line footprint, ~320x140 px) for route or model rows - Three coordinated views inside HUD: quick metrics row, correlation micro-plot, token flow micro-waterfall - Interactions: filter to time window, open detailed route performance, trigger canary rollout, annotate incident - Accessibility: keyboard focus, aria labels, high-contrast color tokens Design constraints and trade-offs: - Must be legible at small sizes; we trade absolute chart granularity for signal clarity (use aggregation and outlier shading) - Minimize data calls: rely on pre-aggregated route-model micro-timeseries from telemetry service; fall back to cached snapshot when latency > 1s - Visual language must align with existing Console tokens but introduce a denser micro-card visual style for per-row embedding User stories: 1) As an SRE, I want to see if rising token counts correspond to higher tail latency for a given route so I can decide to enable KV cache. 2) As a product engineer, I want a persistent pin to surface the top 5 expensive routes on my console homepage. 3) As an ops lead, I want a single-click path from anomaly in HUD to open a canary rollout flow. Deliverables: - Figma prototype (compact HUD component, variants for model vs route contexts) - Chart specs for correlation micro-plot, token flow waterfall, and compact sparkline - Interaction spec and accessibility checklist - Handoff-ready tokens and CSS variables Acceptance criteria listed below.
charts: Correlation micro-plot: Scatter + density band showing median latency (y-axis) vs avg tokens per-request (x-axis). Point size = request volume; color = cost-per-token tier. Must support hover card with p50/p95/p99 latency, avg tokens, total cost, sample request id. Render budget: <25ms client-side draw at HUD mount.

Token flow micro-waterfall: Stacked waterfall representing prefix tokens vs generated tokens vs cached tokens; shows delta cost per segment. Compact bars with stacked hover that expands into timeline. Supports threshold shading for cache miss ratio > 30%.

Mini-sparkline: 60s rolling latency sparkline (p50/p95 overlay) rendered as dual-line compact sparkline with small dot for latest point and a low-opacity band for variance. On hover show exact timestamps and token counts.
Cost needle: Single numeric KPI with micro delta (▲/▼) vs prior window; color-coded by absolute monthly impact. Tooltip: breakdown by model variant and region.
Request sampler: Tiny list (max 3) of sampled request IDs with quick-open to trace and to GitHub-linked evaluation if available.
acceptance_criteria:
1) HUD renders in route list rows and route detail flyout with correct responsive sizing.
2) Correlation micro-plot correctly maps tokens->latency and exposes hovercards with p50/p95/p99 and cost values.
3) Token waterfall highlights cached tokens and computes cost deltas exactly matching backend aggregation within 1%.
4) Interactions: pin, open trace, start canary rollout are wired to Console actions (click handlers documented) and tested.
5) Performance: initial HUD renders within 220ms on desktop and falls back to cached snapshot when telemetry response >1s.
6) Accessibility: keyboard and screen-reader checks pass with ARIA labels and contrast ratio >=4.5:1 for critical text.

2025-02-21 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed wireframes, requested an action path from HUD to canary rollout. Added acceptance criteria to include one-click rollout start. Marked medium customer impact given some pilot customers requested this.

2025-02-24 - Ethan Brooks (Eng lead): Feasibility note: backend can provide pre-aggregated micro-timeseries but sampling window is 30s; suggested adding a fallback cached snapshot. Also called out GPU-heavy compute for density bands — recommendation to precompute density on telemetry side.

2025-02-26 - Design review meeting: Agreed on micro-plot as scatter + density band rather than heatmap to preserve point-level samples. Decision: use request volume for point size rather than color to avoid color overload. Action: update Figma and specs by 2025-03-02.
2025-03-01 - Security review (informal): Confirmed no PII is exposed in HUD samples; must ensure sampled request ids are hashed when surfaced externally. Added to handoff notes.
2025-03-02 - Maya Chen: Updated spec to include ARIA attributes and keyboard interactions. Marked ticket In Review and created prototype link for stakeholders.
notes: Follow-up: schedule a pilot with 2 enterprise customers to validate cost-tier color semantics and check production render times under load. Coordinate with Research/Applied ML on how density bands are computed and stored.
